observations: Two large black plastic tanks are shown in both photos.
The tanks have a ribbed design and are mounted on concrete blocks or a curb.
Photo 0 shows one tank standing upright, the other lying on its side.
Photo 1 shows two tanks strapped to the roof of a white car, with one tank on top and one below.
The tanks appear to be made of thick plastic, possibly HDPE, with visible wear and dirt.
The tanks are not labeled with capacity or model numbers in the photos.
The seller claims 'Top quality Rubber Tank and reservoir' and 'Food grade, used only once for clean water. No crack, no leak, lids complete.'
The tanks are not shown in use, and no interior or bottom details are visible.

claims.claim: Top quality Rubber Tank and reservoir
claims.evidence: The tanks appear to be made of thick plastic, but 'rubber' is not visually confirmed. The material is not clearly rubber, and 'top quality' is subjective and not verifiable from photos.

claims.claim: Food grade, used only once for clean water. No crack, no leak, lids complete.
claims.evidence: No photo shows this; it is the seller's word only.

risks.risk: The tanks may not be food-grade or may have been used for non-food purposes.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the tank's interior or a label indicating food-grade certification.
risks.if_unproven: priced as non-food-grade or used for non-food purposes

risks.risk: The tanks may have cracks, leaks, or structural damage not visible from the outside.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the tank's interior, bottom, and seams, or a video showing the tank being filled and drained.
risks.if_unproven: priced as potentially leaking or structurally compromised

risks.risk: The tanks may not be made of rubber as claimed, but of plastic.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of the tank's material texture or a label indicating the material type.

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the tank's interior to check for cracks or residue.
Photo of any labels or markings indicating food-grade certification or material type.
Video or photo showing the tank being filled and drained to check for leaks.
Photo of the tank's bottom and seams to check for damage.
response.reason: The item is known from the photos. What they cannot prove is priced at its worst case until the proof asked for below arrives.
